title: Conservation, $\mathbb{Z}$-grading, and the $\chi = -6$ constraint on lepton number
html:
Remark. Conservation, \mathbb{Z}-grading, and the \chi = -6 constraint on lepton number

The categorical lepton number possesses several structural properties.

Each beta decay applies the Skein relation at one crossing. This produces a smoothing L_0^{\pm}. It contains exactly one lepton–antilepton pair. Lepton number counts these smoothings.

Each smoothing L_0^{\pm} contributes:

  • One charged lepton (T_{2,3} or T_{2,3}^{\sigma}) with lepton number +1.
  • One neutrino or antineutrino (K_{0_1} or K_{0_1}^{\sigma}) with lepton number -1.

The net lepton number of each L_0^{\pm} pair is zero.

Conservation. Lepton number is conserved by construction:

  1. Skein smoothings produce lepton pairs with net lepton number 0. The nuclear sector loses one crossing. Hadrons carry lepton number 0. The total is \Delta L = 0.
  2. Gröbner–Shirshov re-reduction acts within the Iwahori–Hecke algebra. It produces no smoothings. The total is \Delta L = 0.
  3. Markov moves change the braid representative but not the link type. The total is \Delta L = 0.

Every process expressed as a sequence of Skein relations and Hecke reductions conserves lepton number.

Lepton number is not a \mathbb{Z}-grading (proved). An earlier version of this section asserted that the Skein module \mathcal{K}(S^3; q) admits a natural \mathbb{Z}-grading by the smoothing count, with the nuclear sector in grade 0 and each smoothing shifting the grade by +1. That is false, and the obstruction is proved sorry-free in QOU/StandardModel/LeptonNumberGradingObstruction.lean.

The skein relation is inhomogeneous for such a grading. Writing it as

  L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})\,L_0 ,

the left-hand side is a difference of grade-g classes, hence grade g, while the right-hand side carries one further smoothing, hence grade g+1 (scalars are grade-preserving). An element lying in two distinct homogeneous components is 0, so the relation forces (q - q^{-1})L_0 = 0 and L_+ = L_-. Imposing the grading therefore annihilates every smoothing: it would make lepton number identically 0, which is the one value it cannot take.

This is a scope-(b) exclusion of one construction, with its invariant cited (the defining disjointness of homogeneous components); it does not touch lepton number itself, the Skein module, or the Y = B - L route.

What this leaves, and where L does live. An inhomogeneous relation is what a filtration tolerates rather than a grading, but the corpus's Vassiliev filtration (QOU/KnotTheory/Vassiliev/) grades invariants v : K \to R, not states, so it does not by itself supply a state-valued L.

The carrier is the braid word, not the knot type. This is forced: QOU/StandardModel/LeptonNumberCarrierChirality.lean proves L cannot factor through the unframed knot type, since the mirror must move the carrier and the unknot is amphichiral. It is also what the corpus already does -- AntiparticleCrossingReversalContext takes the mirror to be \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} on braid words and records that it preserves the knot type.

The braid words are fixed by the \chi = -6 constraint below: T(2,n) is the closure of \sigma_1^n, so \nu_e = \sigma_1, e^- = \sigma_1^3, and the antiparticles are \sigma_1^{-1}, \sigma_1^{-3} --- distinct braid words that both close to the unknot, which is exactly how the mirror acts freely. QOU/StandardModel/ChiralFermionBraidWords.lean proves the writhes from the words and shows the candidate

  L(\beta) = \mathrm{sign}\bigl(\mathrm{writhe}(\beta)\bigr)

reproduces every row of the table below, hadrons included. It is a candidate, not a derivation: \mathrm{sign} is a choice of function, the quark braid word is still absent from the corpus, and chirality (u_L vs u_R) is not yet represented.

And it is refuted, under both readings of the gauge freedom.

Markov II. Stabilisation raises the writhe by 1 without changing the link, so L jumps from 0 to 1 on the baryon --- violating conservation clause 3 above, which requires \Delta L = 0 under Markov moves (leptonNumber_not_markov_invariant).

The minimal-level ruling. The escape from the first refutation was that states are Gröbner--Shirshov normal forms, with the observable evaluated at the lowest level of the substrate tower. That closes the escape rather than opening it. The table above assigns \nu_e = K_{0_1} = T_{2,1}, the unknot, whose braid index is 1: its minimal-level normal form is the empty word, and so is its mirror's. At the level where the framework says observables live, \nu_e and \nu_e^{\sigma} are the same state, and no function of the state can give them +1 and -1 --- quite apart from \mathrm{sign}(0) = 0 \neq +1. This is QOU/StandardModel/WritheLevelParity.lean's leptonNumber_collapses_at_minimal_level, and it is the same obstruction LeptonNumberCarrierChirality.lean proved for the unframed knot type, reappearing once the canonical representative is pinned.

So the "carrier is the braid word, not the knot type" escape is unavailable at minimal level, where the braid word is determined by the knot type. Scope-(a): L = \mathrm{sign}(w) is refuted; lepton number itself and the Y = B - L route are untouched, and what the refutation locates is that L must come from data the writhe does not carry --- the framing or the smoothing history, not the crossing sum. See beans qou-kl39, qou-qia8.

Individual lepton assignments.

Particle Knot type Lepton number L Origin
e^- T_{2,3} (trefoil) +1 L_0^{-} charged component (\beta^-)
e^+ T_{2,3}^{\sigma} (mirror trefoil) -1 L_0^{+} charged component (\beta^+)
\nu_e K_{0_1} (unknot) +1 L_0^{+} neutral component (\beta^+)
\nu_e^{\sigma} K_{0_1}^{\sigma} (mirror unknot) -1 L_0^{-} neutral component (\beta^-)

The charged lepton carries L = \pm 1. The neutrino carries L = \mp 1. Each pair sums to zero.

The \chi = -6 constraint. In the Descartes universe, the Euler characteristic \chi(A) = -6 constrains Bring's surface. The torus knot generators T(2, n) with odd n \leq 7 exhaust the fermion spectrum. The electron (T_{2,3}) and neutrino (K_{0_1} = T_{2,1}) are the lowest torus knots in this sequence. The smoothing L_0^{-} must decompose into exactly these knot types. They are the only single-component closures of a 2-arc resolution at a Borromean crossing.

Structural origin of lepton-number conservation. In the Standard Model, lepton number conservation is an accidental symmetry. Here, it is a structural invariant. The Skein relation is the unique operation that changes crossing type. It always produces exactly one lepton pair. The Iwahori–Hecke algebra contains no mechanism to produce an odd number of leptons. The smoothing is a topological operation on a single crossing. Each smoothing is binary.

Lepton number violation requires a process that changes crossing type without passing through the Skein relation. Such a process must exist outside the Iwahori–Hecke algebra. In the \chi = -6 universe, no such process exists.
